papers.title: A block tangential Lanczos method for model reduction of large-scale first and second order dynamical systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a new approach for model reduction of large scale first and second order dynamical systems with multiple inputs and multiple outputs (MIMO). This approach is based on the projection of the initial problem onto tangential Krylov subspaces to produce a simpler reduced-order model that approximates well the behavior of the original model. We present an algorithm named: Adaptive Block Tangential Lanczos-type (ABTL) algorithm. We give some algebraic properties and present some numerical experiences to show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及大规模动力系统的模型降阶，但未涉及生物力学或植入物设计，且缺乏不确定性量化。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modeling for biomedical implants, lacks uncertainty quantification, and does not handle constraints or optimization.

summary_en.motivation: To reduce the computational cost of simulating large-scale first and second order dynamical systems with multiple inputs and outputs.
summary_en.method: An Adaptive Block Tangential Lanczos-type algorithm is proposed to project the original system onto tangential Krylov subspaces for model order reduction.
summary_en.result: The proposed algorithm demonstrates effectiveness in producing accurate reduced-order models as shown by numerical experiments.
summary_en.validation: Numerical benchmarks on standard dynamical system examples.
